root_cause.text: In KVM arm64 nested Stage-2 MMU handling, `kvm_vcpu_init_nested()` could reallocate and free `kvm->arch.nested_mmus[]` under only `config_lock` even though that array is concurrently walked under `kvm->mmu_lock` (including MMU notifier paths), creating a use-after-free race.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description says `kvm->arch.nested_mmus[] is walked under kvm->mmu_lock ... which can run at any time` while `kvm_vcpu_init_nested() reallocates the array and frees the old buffer while holding only kvm->arch.config_lock, so such a walker can reference the freed array`; the patch fixes this by moving the reassign/copy under `write_lock(&kvm->mmu_lock)` and freeing the old buffer only after unlocking.

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: In KVM arm64 nested Stage-2 MMU handling, `kvm_vcpu_init_nested()` could reallocate and free `kvm->arch.nested_mmus[]` under only `config_lock` even though that array is concurrently walked under `kvm->mmu_lock` (including MMU notifier paths), creating a use-after-free race.
agent_logs.evidence_points: The CVE description says `kvm->arch.nested_mmus[] is walked under kvm->mmu_lock ... which can run at any time` while `kvm_vcpu_init_nested() reallocates the array and frees the old buffer while holding only kvm->arch.config_lock, so such a walker can reference the freed array`; the patch fixes this by moving the reassign/copy under `write_lock(&kvm->mmu_lock)` and freeing the old buffer only after unlocking.

intent_record.intent_summary: Expand nested MMU storage safely under lock while preserving and fixing back-pointers during reallocation.
intent_record.what: The code no longer always reallocates `kvm->arch.nested_mmus` with `kvrealloc()` and swaps it unconditionally. Instead, it only allocates a new array when `num_mmus` exceeds `kvm->arch.nested_mmus_size`, uses `kvcalloc()` for the new buffer, takes `kvm->mmu_lock` with `write_lock()`, copies the old array into the new one with `memcpy()`, updates each copied `pgt->mmu` back-pointer to point into the new array, swaps the pointers, unlocks, and frees the old buffer via `kvfree(tmp)`. The subsequent initialization loop remains, starting from the previous `nested_mmus_size` up to `num_mmus`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, existing nested MMU entries are preserved while the array is expanded only when needed. The lock makes the pointer swap and back-pointer updates safe against concurrent MMU access, and the copied structures keep their `pgt->mmu` references valid after relocation. This avoids stale back-pointers and ensures newly added nested MMUs are initialized in the enlarged array.

grouping_result.intent: Expand nested MMU storage safely under lock while preserving and fixing back-pointers during reallocation.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it addresses unsafe reallocation of kvm->arch.nested_mmus[] by expanding nested MMU storage safely under lock and fixing back-pointers, which is the race leading to the use-after-free.

candidates.rationale: This reallocates the nested MMU array, which can move or free the old allocation while it may still be walked under kvm->mmu_lock, creating the use-after-free race described in the root cause.
Swapping in the newly reallocated array under only config_lock changes the backing storage of nested_mmus without synchronizing with mmu_lock readers, directly enabling concurrent UAF.

vuln_statements.explanation: This reallocation can move or free the existing nested_mmus array while other paths may still walk it under kvm->mmu_lock, creating the use-after-free race.
Swapping in the reallocated array under only config_lock changes the backing storage concurrently visible to mmu_lock readers, directly exposing the UAF race.

bic_trace_step.reason: The shown function already contains the reallocation fix. The key change is `swap(kvm->arch.nested_mmus, tmp);`, which makes the KVM struct point to the newly allocated array before initialization continues, avoiding leaving a stale pointer on failure. The code then uses the new array consistently: `kvm->arch.nested_mmus[i].pgt->mmu = &kvm->arch.nested_mmus[i];`, `init_nested_s2_mmu(kvm, &kvm->arch.nested_mmus[i]);`, and `kvm_free_stage2_pgd(&kvm->arch.nested_mmus[i]);`. It also no longer assigns `kvm->arch.nested_mmus = tmp;` at the end, so the vulnerable stale-pointer reallocation path described in the root cause is absent here.
